title: Water systems for medical device manufacturing | Aquemi
meta: Rinse and process water systems for medical device makers, with endotoxin and bioburden limits set from product risk and documented for ISO 13485 audits.
headline: Rinse water you can defend in your cleaning validation
lead: For many devices, the last thing to touch the product before packaging is water. We design Purified Water and Water for Injection (WFI) systems whose quality matches your product's risk, with records that fit an ISO 13485 quality system.

body: There is no single water standard for device manufacturing. You set the water quality from what the device contacts and how it is finished.

A non-sterile device for intact skin may need only Purified Water (PW). An implant or a device that contacts blood is often rinsed in low-endotoxin water, because residual endotoxin on the device counts against its release limit. We help you document that decision.

blocks.caption: Reference limits · device and rinse water
blocks.note: Device endotoxin limits apply to the finished device, not the water. They are listed because rinse water quality is chosen to protect them.

rows.p: Device endotoxin limit, cerebrospinal fluid contact

items.d: Reverse osmosis (RO) with electrodeionization (EDI) for washing and rinsing.
Low-endotoxin final rinse without the energy cost of distillation.
Loops to washers and cleanroom points of use.
Matched to your feedwater to protect the RO.
Continuous conductivity and TOC with audit-trailed records.
Short, high-flow draws. We size storage and loop pressure for them.
Water quality at the washer inlet is part of your validated process. We provide points to sample it.
Where a device contains a drug, pharmaceutical GMP expectations for water may also apply.
Our documents map to ISO 13485 records for equipment, calibration and change control.

items.a: Only if your risk assessment says rinse water endotoxin must be controlled to that level. Many device makers use PW with an endotoxin specification instead.

items.q: Is this the same as water for reprocessing devices in hospitals?
items.a: No. Hospital reprocessing follows AAMI ST108 and CSA Z314. This page covers water used to manufacture devices.

items.q: Will our auditor accept your qualification documents?
items.a: They are written to GAMP 5 and fit an ISO 13485 system. Your quality unit approves them before execution.

cta.h: Match the water to the device
cta.body: Tell us what your devices contact and how they are cleaned, and we will propose a water grade and a system.
